activity.overview: Read a model opinion piece and find each of its parts.
activity.passage:
Our School Needs a Garden
by a fourth grader

I think our school should plant a garden in the empty space behind the gym. A garden would help us learn, help us eat well, and make our school more beautiful.

First, a garden is an outdoor classroom. We could measure how fast bean plants grow in math and watch the life cycle of a plant in science. For example, last year my cousin's class grew sunflowers and charted their height every week.

Also, kids who grow vegetables are more likely to try them. When I grew tomatoes with my grandmother, I ate them right off the vine, even though I used to hate tomatoes. A school garden could give every student that chance.

Finally, right now the space behind the gym is just dirt and weeds. Flowers and vegetables would make it a place people want to visit.

For all these reasons, a garden would make our school a better place to learn and grow. Let's dig in!

questions.prompt: What is the writer's opinion? Copy the sentence that states it.
List the three reasons the writer gives.
What example supports the reason about learning outdoors?
Find three linking words or phrases the writer uses to connect ideas.
How does the conclusion restate the opinion?
Which reason is most convincing to you? Explain why, and say what evidence would make another reason stronger.

sentenceFrames: The most convincing reason is ___ because ___.
